title: Acute chest-pain routing
baselineFacts: An adult reports abrupt central chest pressure with sweating that began forty minutes ago.
The originating setting is an outpatient clinic without cardiac monitoring or emergency imaging capability.
The decision owner is the clinic physician deciding whether to transfer immediately or continue local evaluation.

validEvidence.text: A new tracing shows persistent ST elevation across two contiguous anterior leads during ongoing pain.

irrelevantEvidence.text: The clinic waiting room temperature was recorded as seventy degrees during the same afternoon visit.

title: Improving localized rash
baselineFacts: An adult has a small localized itchy rash after changing laundry detergent, without breathing symptoms.
The originating setting is primary care with routine follow-up available the same week.
The decision owner is the primary-care physician deciding whether specialist escalation is required now.

validEvidence.text: Serial photographs over seven days show the localized rash fading without fever, mucosal lesions, or spread.

irrelevantEvidence.text: The patient completed sixteen pages of intake paperwork using a blue pen before the scheduled appointment.

title: Acute focal neurologic deficit
baselineFacts: An older adult developed sudden facial asymmetry and difficulty lifting one arm twenty minutes ago.
The originating setting is a rural clinic without CT imaging or thrombolysis capability.
The decision owner is the clinic physician choosing emergency transfer versus continued local observation.

validEvidence.text: A witnessed examination confirms new unilateral arm drift and speech difficulty persisting at reassessment.

irrelevantEvidence.text: A registration clerk confirms the patient arrived wearing a gray jacket and carrying two keys.

title: Unreliable isolated laboratory result
baselineFacts: An asymptomatic adult has one unexpectedly high potassium value from a difficult blood draw.
The originating setting is primary care with repeat phlebotomy available within hours.
The decision owner is the primary-care physician choosing immediate specialist escalation versus obtaining confirmatory evidence.

validEvidence.text: The only potassium result came from a visibly hemolyzed sample, and no repeat measurement is available.

irrelevantEvidence.text: The laboratory waiting area contains four chairs, one clock, and a recently replaced ceiling light.

title: Severe hypertension during pregnancy
baselineFacts: A pregnant adult late in gestation reports a new severe headache and visual disturbance.
The originating setting is an outpatient office without continuous maternal or fetal monitoring.
The decision owner is the office physician choosing emergency transfer versus routine follow-up.

validEvidence.text: Two correctly sized cuff readings fifteen minutes apart both show blood pressure above severe-range thresholds.

irrelevantEvidence.text: Two wall calendars in adjacent rooms both display the correct month and the same holiday markings.

title: Stable uncomplicated reflux symptoms
baselineFacts: An adult reports intermittent burning after meals that improves with routine first-line measures.
The originating setting is primary care with scheduled reassessment and no current alarm features reported.
The decision owner is the primary-care physician choosing specialist referral now versus continued routine management.

validEvidence.text: A structured review confirms stable weight, normal swallowing, no bleeding, and symptom improvement over four weeks.

irrelevantEvidence.text: A structured inventory confirms four magazines, three clipboards, two lamps, and one clock in reception.

title: Head injury with anticoagulant exposure
baselineFacts: An older adult taking a prescribed anticoagulant fell and struck the head one hour ago.
The originating setting is urgent care without CT imaging or prolonged neurologic observation capability.
The decision owner is the urgent-care physician choosing emergency transfer versus discharge.

validEvidence.text: Medication reconciliation confirms the anticoagulant dose was taken today, and new vomiting began during observation.

irrelevantEvidence.text: Supply reconciliation confirms the examination room has fresh paper, and new pencils arrived during observation.

title: Uncharacterized possible anemia
baselineFacts: An adult reports nonspecific fatigue without syncope, active bleeding, chest pain, or measured vital abnormalities.
The originating setting is primary care, and no blood count or iron studies are available.
The decision owner is the primary-care physician choosing specialist escalation versus obtaining basic diagnostic evidence.

validEvidence.text: The record confirms no blood count, reticulocyte measure, iron study, or symptom chronology has been obtained.

irrelevantEvidence.text: The office confirms each hallway sign, waiting-room map, doorway label, and appointment card was recently updated.
